Understanding the JavaScript Event Loop

The event loop is what allows JavaScript to perform non-blocking operations, despite the fact that JavaScript is single-threaded, by offloading operations to the system kernel whenever possible.

Microtasks such as promise callbacks run before the next macrotask. This is why a resolved promise logs before a setTimeout callback with zero delay, which surprises many developers.

Understanding starvation: if microtasks keep queueing more microtasks, rendering never gets a chance to happen and the page freezes.
